info.title: WiSAR Terrain-Aware Range Rings API
info.summary: Headless API for Terrain-Aware Range Rings (TARR) and travel-time isochrones.
info.description:
Computes Terrain-Aware Range Rings (Koester percentile envelopes) and travel-time isochrones from an Initial Planning Point (IPP) over an anisotropic cost surface (Tobler slope, NLCD land cover, OSM trails/roads, NHD hydrography). Intended client: CloudTAK plugins (Incident Manager, Search Containment).

## Workflow (asynchronous request-reply)
1. `POST /tarr/jobs` or `POST /travel-time/jobs` → `202 Accepted` with a `Location` header and a Job.
2. Poll `GET /jobs/{job_id}` (honour `Retry-After`) until `status` is `succeeded` or `failed`.
3. Fetch outputs from the links in `outputs`.

Jobs run one at a time, first in first out. An analysis takes roughly 15 s to several minutes.

## Conventions
- Coordinates: WGS84. Request bodies use named `lat`/`lon`; GeoJSON follows RFC 7946 (`[lon, lat]`).
- Rasters: EPSG:4326 Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF, DEFLATE, lossless, with overviews. Grid is capped at 1000×1000 cells, so large analyses have coarser cells; see `result.cell_size_m`.
- Distances in kilometres unless a `unit` field says otherwise. Times in hours.
- Errors: RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`.
- Land cover and hydrography snapshots cover CONUS; outside it the analysis runs with warnings (see `result.warnings`).

## Authentication
Send the caller's CloudTAK token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. WiSAR verifies it with CloudTAK `GET /api/login` and caches the result briefly. `/health`, `/openapi.json` and `/docs` are public.

## Retention
Finished jobs and their outputs are deleted after `WISAR_JOB_TTL_HOURS` (default 72). `expires_at` gives the time. Copy anything you need to keep into the mission.

This tool is one input to search planning and does not replace the judgment of search planners or incident command.

get.description: Liveness, queue state and data snapshot freshness. No authentication.
Every installed profile dataset with its categories, eco-region/terrain variants, p25/p50/p75 distances and calibration multipliers. Use this to populate subject pickers.

One section of the WiSAR web tool's reference content, read from its static/index.html at request time, so it follows upstream updates. `html` is the section body as an HTML fragment: the web tool's markup and inline styles, with its Close/Got it button, scripts, form controls and inline event handlers removed. The inline styles use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--text-secondary)`); `css_variables` gives the web tool's values for the ones used, so a client can set them on the element it renders into. The colours were chosen for a dark background.

Sections: `metadata`, `changelog`, `validation`, `tarr-explainer` ("What's a TARR?"), `travel-time-explainer` ("What's Travel Time?"), and `scope-note` (the note under the mode choice on the web tool's start screen).

Responses carry an `ETag`; send it back in `If-None-Match` to get `304 Not Modified` when the page has not changed.

304.description: Not modified since the ETag sent in If-None-Match.

503.description: The web tool page is missing, the section was not found in it (renamed upstream), or CloudTAK could not be reached to verify the token.

post.description: Queues a TARR analysis. The subject is either a **listed** profile (the server resolves distances from the dataset and applies its calibration) or a **custom** profile with caller-supplied p25/p50/p75. Analysis radius is calibrated p75 + 2 km.
Queues a travel-time (isochrone) analysis. Travel time per cell = cost-distance ÷ base speed. Analysis radius is max(`min_radius_m`, base speed × longest interval + 2 km).

get.description: Unexpired jobs created by the calling CloudTAK user, newest first.
Any authenticated user holding the job id can read it, so a job can be shared within an incident.

Retry-After.description: Suggested seconds before polling again. Present while queued or running.

delete.description: Removes a queued or finished job and its outputs. Only the user who created the job may delete it. A running job cannot be interrupted (409).

403.description: Caller did not create this job.

get.description: TARR percentile polygons or travel-time isochrones as an RFC 7946 FeatureCollection.

409.description: Job has not succeeded (still queued or running, or it failed).

get.description: The same polygons as KML 2.2, styled with the contour colours.

409.description: Job has not succeeded (still queued or running, or it failed).

get.description: Float32. Cumulative anisotropic travel cost from the IPP in flat-ground-equivalent metres. Travel hours = value ÷ (speed_kmh × 1000). NoData −9999.

409.description: Job has not succeeded (still queued or running, or it failed).

get.description: Float32. Per-cell friction multiplier (1.0 = trail/road). NoData −9999.

409.description: Job has not succeeded (still queued or running, or it failed).

get.description: Float32, 0–1. Per-cell Jacobs (2015) terrain-attractor strength: max of stream-trail intersection 1.00, trail 0.55, low-elevation pocket 0.35, stream 0.28, high-elevation prominence 0.18. The web tool's heatmap as data. NoData −9999.

409.description: Job has not succeeded (still queued or running, or it failed).

get.description: Float32 band class: 4 = inside p25, 3 = p25–p50, 2 = p50–p75, 1 = beyond p75, 0 = NoData. TARR jobs only; a travel-time job returns 404.

409.description: Job has not succeeded (still queued or running, or it failed).

cloudtakBearer.description: CloudTAK user token, verified against CloudTAK GET /api/login.

JobId.name: job_id
JobId.description: Job id returned when the job was created.

BadRequest.description: Body is not valid JSON or is not an object.

Unprocessable.description: Body failed validation. `errors` lists each field.

NotFound.description: No such job (or no such output for this job type).

Gone.description: Job expired and its outputs were deleted.

AuthUnavailable.description: CloudTAK could not be reached to verify the token.

Unavailable.description: Queue is full, or CloudTAK could not be reached to verify the token.

pointer.description: JSON Pointer into the request body, e.g. /subject/distances/p50.

Distances.description: Find distances; must be strictly increasing and positive.

eco_region.description: e.g. Dry, Temperate, Urban. Null or omitted = default.

terrain.description: e.g. Mountainous, Flat. Null or omitted = default.

ListedSubject.description: Resolved like the web tool: exact eco_region+terrain, else eco_region with default terrain, else the category default. `resolved.variant` in the Job shows which one was used.

Calibration.description: `auto`: listed subject gets the dataset's per-category multipliers (or the dataset default); custom subject gets none. `global`: apply the dataset default multipliers. `none`: use distances as given. The Job's `resolved` block always shows multipliers and final km.

dataset.description: Dataset id from GET /profiles. Used for listed subjects and for `global` calibration.

Speed.description: Flat-ground base walking speed. Must be > 0 and ≤ 20 km/h (12.4 mph).

intervals_hours.description: Isochrone times in hours. Sorted server-side.

min_radius_m.description: Minimum analysis radius. The server enlarges it to base speed × longest interval + 2 km.

ResolvedTarr.description: How the request was turned into thresholds.

subject_label.description: e.g. "Hiker (Dry, Mountainous)" or the custom name.

min_radius_km.description: min_radius_m from the request, in km.

cell_size_m.description: Approximate cell size. Above ~30 m means the 1000-cell cap coarsened the grid.

queue_position.description: 1 = next to run. Null unless queued.

owner.description: CloudTAK username (email) that created the job.

outputs.description: Present when succeeded. Keys are output names.

geometry.description: GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon, [lon, lat], 5 decimal places.

callsign.description: Display name for TAK, e.g. "25% Percentile TARR" or "4h".

remarks.description: e.g. "Threshold: 2.41 km cost-distance" or "Travel time: 4h at flat-ground speed".

stroke.description: Outline colour (same as color). CloudTAK reads this, not color.

fill-opacity.description: 0.1 for TARR and travel-time rings. Never 0: CloudTAK's GeoJSON import drops a 0 and falls back to a 50% fill.

calibration.description: Category-specific multipliers, or null to use the dataset default.

status.description: degraded = a data snapshot is missing; analyses still run, with warnings.

queue.description: queued counts every waiting analysis, including legacy /api/analyze* calls.

title.description: The section's heading in the web tool.

html.description: HTML fragment with inline styles. No scripts, form controls or event handlers.

css_variables.description: Values of the CSS custom properties the fragment uses, from the web tool's :root.

source.description: Where the section was read from.

element_id.description: id of the modal in the web tool page.

sha256.description: Hash of the page the section came from.
